expectations.text: Explains git-stack does NOT resolve conflicts and hands control back to plain git
expectations.evidence: 'a rebase cannot auto-resolve a real content conflict ... git-stack hands control to a normal git rebase and pauses'.

expectations.text: Walks through resolving with git (edit files, git add, git rebase --continue), or git rebase --abort to bail
expectations.evidence: Steps: edit markers, git add, git rebase --continue (or --skip); bail-out git rebase --abort.

expectations.text: Mentions that after a manual rebase the stack may need `git-stack --repair`, or that branch-stash apply can return to the pre-sync state
expectations.evidence: States 'git branch-stash pop' restores all branch positions to the pre-sync state (the branch-stash branch of the OR); does not mention --repair.

expectations.text: If it mentions branch-stash as the bail-out, targets the `git-stack` stash stack by name, not the default
expectations.evidence: Mentions branch-stash but uses bare 'git branch-stash pop' with no 'git-stack' stack name, targeting the default.

summary: Conflict handling and git-resolution steps correct, but the branch-stash bail-out omits the git-stack stack name.
